messages:
alex: FYI CI SAST job failing on `keystore` lib after I added the new role mapping. Logs point at the authz package, getting a proto deserialization error. anyone seen this?
maria: saw the alert earlier, repro locally. stack trace points to a schema bump in `keystore/audit.proto` — scanner chokes on the unknown field tag.
alex: thanks. it passes unit tests but the SAST aggregator fails in CI. sec-bot: new-sast-alert id=SC-9087 severity=medium rule=proto-deserialization
devops: could be the scanner image in runners. which scanner version are we pinning? `cat .scan/config.yaml` shows 3.2.8 currently.
alex: confirmed CI image is 3.2.8. i patched locally to 3.4.1 and SAST passes. should we bump the scanner image in the runners?
maria: +1 for bump. also QA DAST found a hit on an internal admin endpoint: `/admin/redirect?next=` looks like an open-redirect. not exploitable from internet but risky for internal phishing.
sam: open-redirect on admin is bad for impersonation attacks. mitigation: validate `next` against allowlist and emit an audit event when redirect param present. also rate-limit those endpoints.
jen: on audit storage, if we log to the encrypted audit store, remember our ingest pattern: service only needs `kms.encrypt` and write permissions; decryption is reserved for report jobs. we avoid granting decrypt to the ingest path.
maria: but our compliance reports decrypt events to compute trends. how do reports access plaintext?
jen: reports run as separate jobs with short-lived granted `kms.decrypt` via the key rotation workflow. the report role is tightly scoped and tracked in audit logs. include that in the PR description.
alex: action list: 1) bump scanner to 3.4.1 in `.github/workflows/sast.yml` 2) patch admin redirect validation + tests 3) emit audit event to encrypted store and document RBAC for reporting job.
devops: i'll open PRs: scanner bump + runner image tag update. note: Dedicated clusters will need a rolling restart for updated runner images.
maria: i'll push a tiny redirect validation fix and include a DAST harness test. i can also add a sentinel eval in Redwood Optimize to detect regressions.
sec-bot: incident-ticket created INC-2026; severity=low; owner=maria; due=2026-03-28
sam: low now but flagging: if the fix touches key escrow or key grants, require sec signoff before merge.
alex: tagging @security for review — @jen can you run a quick checklist? we need: RBAC diff, KMS access matrix, audit log schema diff, and a release note.
jen: on it. quick checklist: 1) confirm minimal KMS perms (encrypt-only for ingest account) 2) ensure audit events are append-only and HMAC'd for tamper evidence 3) document key rotation impact on historical report accessibility 4) add rollback/runbook steps for incident response
devops: PRs opened: #4212 (scanner-bump), #4213 (runner image). linking PRs in each pipeline job.
maria: PR #4214 for redirect fix ready for review. includes unit+DAST harness snapshot and a small canary flag.
alex: good. propose canary rollout via feature flag: `admin_redirect_strict` default off, enable in staging for 24h, then gradual customer rollout.
sam: note: routing policy in Dedicated might route to older model variants with different RBAC behavior; include fallback and graceful degradation in the rollout plan.
jen: added KMS PR notes: recommend `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypter` for ingest SA and timebound `cryptoKeyDecrypter` grants for report job with IAM Conditions.
sec-bot: reminder: schedule security review meeting 2026-03-26 09:30 UTC — attendees: alex, maria, jen, devops, sam
alex: ack. i'll prepare a short changelog and a blameless followup note if anything regresses after rollout.
maria: thanks — small but good catch from QA DAST. :thumbsup:
sam: if anyone wants to see the KMS grant dance i can demo in #eng-infra tomorrow.
alex: great. i'll close this thread once all PRs merge and runbook is attached. keep updates here.
